- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp spikes in sentiment or price; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% after a +10%+ spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 0.5–1.0% lag correction if sentiment turns bullish after day 15–20.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to match sentiment swing direction 1–2 days ahead.
